messages:
mina: Heads up — legal handed us a request for raw request/response logs for customer 'AcmeTx'. They want full payloads for an audit. Can we provide something that satisfies them without exposing PII?
jasper: yikes. we shouldn't hand over raw. two quick options: strong redaction + per-tenant HMACs, or a bounded export that uses k-anonymity buckets. both with audit trail.
olivia: agree. also consider an ephemeral inspect token flow for SEs — generates a timeboxed unmask view for specific records instead of bulk export. reduces blast radius. :lock:
kevin: ephemeral inspect is good. question: legal wants timestamps and full prompts. even with HMACs we might leak secrets in prompts. are we ok with hashing prompt text? deterministic hash will let them correlate across records.
sara: maybe provide a reversible masked export under a legal-only KMS key escrow. key ops + legal signoff. but that's heavy and risky.
mina: options list for them: (A) scrub by profile + sample 1% with hashes, (B) ephemeral inspect tokens + audit log, (C) full export under escrow KMS w/ escrow policy. which do we want to recommend?
jasper: pick B as primary. implement a console workflow: "Create Inspect Session" -> select tenant & time range -> auto-generate short-lived URL with explicit justification field. logs a legal ticket id.
olivia: and add a redact profile flag: `scrub_profile: strict|moderate|none`. strict removes anything that looks like ssn/email/creditcard, moderate keeps email domains, etc.
kevin: ergonomics: console should surface estimated leak-risk score before export. simple scale 0-100. compute from heuristics: presence of long strings, numeric-heavy, email regex hits.
ops-oncall: curious about telemetry. if we enable ephemeral inspect, do we change sampling? we can't keep full payloads longer than 7d in primary store. maybe keep a short raw buffer (48h) only for inspect.
mina: yes — propose raw buffer: 48h ephemeral store, default retention 48h, inspect session extends view but not retention. all exports require legal ticket.
ingest-bot: INFO: sampler updated for route /v1/embeddings -> rate=0.01, scrub_profile=moderate (applied 2026-03-19T18:12:00Z)
sara: implementation nit: we should avoid deterministic hashes for prompts. use HMAC with per-tenant salt rotated monthly — helps correlation while limiting cross-tenant linking. document rotation policy in console.
jasper: small config sketch that could live in repo or console (example):
```
route_logging:
  /v1/chat:
    sample_rate: 0.02
    scrub_profile: strict
    raw_buffer_ttl: 48h
    inspect_session_allowed: true
    inspect_justification_required: true
```
kevin: +1. add `risk_score_threshold` to auto-deny exports above X. manual override requires director-level approval.
mina: rollout plan: canary 5% of tenants with inspect UI disabled by default but enabled via per-tenant flag. gather metrics: #inspect_requests, avg risk_score, false_negatives from QA prompt set.
olivia: QA note: create a focused prompt-set that intentionally leaks emails/SSNs to validate scrub profiles. include in CI gating for scrub_profile changes.
ops-oncall: oncall request: if someone abuses inspect token, we need fast revoke + audit push to SSO logs. add a kill-switch in Console.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: scrub-profiles/v2 -> canary tenants [acct-501..acct-525] (sha: a1b2c3d)
mina: thanks. i'll draft a short RFC and a console mockup. tagging @kevin @jasper for review before i loop legal.
kevin: i'll take a pass this afternoon.
jasper: +1. ping when RFC drops.
mina: filing ticket: PLAT-4319. will attach mockups and sample CI test.
sara: and i'll write up the HMAC rotation ops playbook.
mina: awesome. moving to async — if anyone has objections to B (ephemeral inspect) speak now, else i'll proceed.
